w:r.w:t: Modern food delivery websites levy heavy charges on customers and restaurants on every single order. Several reports and analysis, such as that of RetailPOS India indicate that commissions often range between 25% to 30% for the majority of restaurants operating on Swiggy and Zomato. At the same time, many food delivery agents are paid bare minimum wage and do not have the freedom to choose how they are paid for their work.
Our project aims to address these issues by providing all three stakeholders an open, transparent portal to carry out their business.
Customers:- They use the system to browse restaurants, order food, make payments, and track their orders.
Restaurants:- They use the system to manage their menus, receive orders, prepare food, and arrange delivery
Delivery Agents:- They use the system to receive delivery requests, choose their preferred payment method, and complete deliveries.
Payment/Wallet System:- This system handles the virtual transactions between customers, restaurants, and delivery agents.
Map/Location API Providers:- This system uses mapping services to estimate the delivery times and it determines whether restaurants are within the 30 minute delivery range.
The OrderFood system will have three primary user profiles. Each profile will have a different interface and set of functionalities.
Customer:- Customers who want to order food from one or more restaurants.
Restaurant:- Businesses that list their food items on the platform, receive orders, prepare food, and arrange delivery.
Delivery Agent:- Delivery agents are the users who collect prepared orders from restaurants and deliver them to the customers.

This particular system will notify the most affordable available delivery agent first, if the agent rejects the request, another agent will be notified. If all agents reject that request, responsibility for delivery returns to the restaurant.
Interfaces should be simple and easy to understand for customers, restaurants, and delivery agents.
The system should respond quickly when users browse menus, place orders, or accept delivery requests.
Orders and transactions should be processed correctly without loss of information.
User accounts and wallet transactions should be protected from unauthorized access.
The platform should be available whenever customers, restaurants, and delivery agents need to use it.

The system should be capable of supporting an increasing number of users, restaurants, and orders.
The system should be structured so that features and external services can be modified or updated easily.

The most important quality parameters are reliability, security, performance, usability, and accuracy because the system handles food orders, delivery assignments, locations, and financial transactions.
30-Minute Delivery Constraint: Customers should only be able to order from restaurants that are reachable within 30 minutes of their delivery location.
External API Dependency: The system will depend on freely available mapping and location APIs such as Geoapify, Bing Maps, or OpenStreetMap to estimate delivery times.
Separate Transactions: When an order contains food from multiple restaurants, each restaurant's order must be paid for through a separate transaction.
Delivery Agent Availability: A delivery request depends on the availability and acceptance of delivery agents. If all available agents reject the request, the restaurant must handle the delivery.
Delivery Confirmation: Customers must confirm whether their previous order has been delivered before placing another order.
Virtual Wallet System: The project uses an internal/imaginary wallet system for carrying out transactions rather than necessarily implementing a real banking or payment gateway.
Multiple User Interfaces: The system must provide separate but interconnected interfaces for customers, restaurants, and delivery agents.
